'''Neil Michael O'Connell''' is an Irish mathematician from [[Shannon, County Clare]]. He attended [[Trinity College Dublin]], and was elected to scholarship in 1987.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tcdlife.ie/scholars/scholar/about-list.php |title=List of Scholars |website=TCD Scholars |publisher=TCD Life |access-date=2021-01-25}}</ref> He earned his bachelor's degree in mathematics and a gold medal in 1989 and completed an M.Sc. in 1990.<ref name="ucdhomepage" /> He obtained his PhD in 1993 at [[UC Berkeley]] under the supervision of [[Steven Neil Evans]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=34473 |title=Neil Michael O'Connell |website=genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu |publisher=Mathematics Genealogy Project |access-date=2021-01-25}}</ref><ref name="ucdhomepage">{{cite web |url=https://www.ucd.ie/research/people/mathematicsstatistics/professorneilo'connell/ |title=UCD Page for Professor Neil O'Connell |website=www.ucd.ie |publisher=University College Dublin |access-date=2021-01-25}}</ref> He subsequently worked at the [[Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dias.ie/2010/07/09/o-connell-n/ |title=O'Connell, N (Past Members) |website= www.dias.ie |publisher=Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies |access-date=2021-06-03}}</ref> and the [[University of Warwick]].<ref name="ucdhomepage" />

He works in [[probability theory]], in particular [[random matrices]]. He was awarded the inaugural Itô prize in 2002 (together with Ben Hambly and James Martin),<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bernoullisociety.org/index.php/prizes/15-features/157-ito-prize |title=Itô Prize |date=2025-01-29 |website=www.bernoulli-society.org |publisher=Bernoulli Society |access-date=2025-11-14}}</ref> and the [[Rollo Davidson Prize]] in 2005.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/rollo-davidson-trust |title=Rollo Davidson Trust | website=www.statslab.cam.ac.uk |publisher=University of Cambridge Statistical Laboratory |access-date=2021-01-25}}</ref> In 2013 he was Doob Lecturer at the 36th Conference on Stochastic Processes and Their Applications, in Boulder, Colorado.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bernoullisociety.org/index.php/organization/lecture-selection-committee |title=Schramm/Doob Lecture Selection Committee |date=2025-07-07 |website=www.bernoulli-society.org |publisher=Bernoulli Society |access-date=2025-11-14}}</ref> He is currently Professor at [[University College Dublin]].<ref name="ucdhomepage" />
